01-phillips-curve.text: In the static model the unemployment coefficient is -0.002, with no stars: there is no static trade-off.
In the dynamic model, lagged inflation has a coefficient of 0.389.
Unemployment is significant at the 5% level in the dynamic model, with a coefficient of 0.007.
Expectations dominate: the Focus coefficient is 0.686, significant at 1%.
The test of gamma + delta = 1 gives p = 0.432, which proves that the long-run Phillips curve is vertical.
The Durbin-Watson statistic of the static model is 1.927.
With Newey-West errors the standard error on the expectation term rises from 0.111 to 0.177, and the coefficient stays significant.
HAC errors change the estimates: the expectation coefficient falls from 0.686 to 0.177.

01-phillips-curve.text: The dynamic model raises R² from 0.000 to 0.421 on 169 monthly observations.

02-crime-panel.text: Pooled OLS gives an elasticity of the crime rate with respect to the probability of arrest of -0.633.
In the two-way fixed-effects model, a 1% higher probability of arrest goes with a crime rate 0.360 percentage points lower.
County fixed effects shrink the arrest coefficient to -0.359.
Clustering by county raises the standard error on police per capita from 0.027 to 0.093.
Clustering by county changes the police coefficient from 0.422 to 0.093.

02-crime-panel.text: More police per capita reduces crime: the two-way fixed-effects coefficient is 0.422.
02-crime-panel.planted: positive sign read as a reduction, causal wording

02-crime-panel.text: The White test (LM = 410.04, p < 0.0001) rejects homoskedasticity.
Because the arrest coefficient is significant (-0.360), the panel shows that arrests cause crime to fall.
The panel has 630 observations and the pooled R² is 0.805.

03-religion-and-domestic-violence.text: With state fixed effects and HC1 errors, the evangelical-density coefficient is 0.0009 (SE 0.0009).
Evangelical density significantly increases recorded domestic violence (coefficient 0.0009).
Adding the non-domestic notification proxy raises R² to 0.404.
The Poisson model with a population offset gives a coefficient of 0.0080, an incidence-rate ratio of 1.0081.
The Poisson IRR of 1.0081 means each extra point of evangelical density goes with 100.81% more recorded cases.
Notification intensity matters: the proxy coefficient is 0.4237 and significant at 1%.
Since the coefficient is not significant, the paper proves that evangelical density has no effect on domestic violence.
